entries.title: Injury-ridden Blackhawks ride Spencer Knight to fourth consecutive win
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a>’ only viable formula to beat the Rangers on Friday was obvious well before the puck dropped.</p><p>With a lineup <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/27/blackhawks-patrick-kane-injury-update-bowen-byram-connor-bedard" target="_blank" >decimated by injuries</a>, they needed to find some offense from unlikely sources and rely on surging goalie Spencer Knight to tip the scale.</p><p>That’s exactly how it played out. The Hawks earned their fourth consecutive victory by grinding out a 2-1 decision in front of a season-high sellout crowd of 20,302 at the United Center.</p><p>They did it with only 10 shots on goal, their fewest in a regular-season game since the NHL began tracking that stat in 1959. The only previous instance came in a 1974 playoff victory against the Kings.</p><p>The Rangers, meanwhile, fired 31 shots on Knight, but only one shot beat him — and none did in the final two periods.</p><p>Knight has <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/24/blackhawks-spencer-knight-warning-odd-man-rushes-workload" target="_blank" >found his A-game</a> in the last few weeks, going 5-1-1 with a .922 save percentage in his last seven starts. His plus-6.3 goals saved above average during that span ranks second-best in the league, trailing only Islanders star Ilya Sorokin.</p><p>‘‘We did a pretty good job of bending and not breaking,’’ coach Jeff Blashill said. ‘‘We had a lot of blocks. We defended hard around the net.</p><p>‘‘[We’re] not giving up some of the super-A-quality chances we were earlier in the year. You’re giving up more contested stuff. That’s the way you have to do it to give your goalie a chance to be great, and he was great.’’</p><p>Knight mentioned the Hawks’ long flight home from Seattle on Thanksgiving — which prevented them from practicing the day before a matinee, like usual — might have handicapped their performance, but it clearly didn’t handicap his.</p><p>‘‘People sometimes evaluate goaltending just based on results, but I think there’s a lot of times you can find good or bad in good or bad games,’’ Knight said. ‘‘There’s things I did wrong today. There’s things I did really well in the games I’ve given up four.’’</p><p>Andrew Mangiapane provided all the Hawks’ production with two power-play goals in the first period. Both times, he slipped unnoticed into the right side of the slot and, after taking passes from Oliver Moore and Ryan Donato, got the puck off his quickly.</p><p>Mangiapane certainly counts as an unlikely source of offense. Although he’s a relentless forechecker, he entered the day with zero goals in 12 games and had received zero seconds of ice time on the power play.</p><p>‘‘[It was] a little bit of a shock when I came in this morning and saw I was on the power play,’’ Mangiapane said. ‘‘[I] felt good, though.’’</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">GOAL: Donato to Andrew Mangiapane who has his second power-play goal of the period. <a href="https://t.co/zAtUeRftpm">pic.twitter.com/zAtUeRftpm</a></p>— BHF (@BlackhawksFocus) <a href="https://x.com/BlackhawksFocus/status/2126455462757310502?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 27, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>The Hawks, already missing three of their top six scorers, finally dodged one injury bullet. Top scorer Roman Kantserov left during the second period with an apparent hand or wrist issue but returned unaffected for the third.</p><p>Even with Kantserov, it will be difficult to cook with this recipe very often. Talent matters in this league, even if it can be overcome on a day-to-day basis, and the Wild will pose an especially tough challenge Sunday.</p><p>Among the forwards, the Hawks will need Frank Nazar and Moore to remain productive without Patrick Kane, need Anton Frondell to find a rhythm again and need more from Ryan Greene, who struggled Friday and doesn’t have a point since Halloween.</p><p>Blashill seems encouraged, however, that the Hawks are executing their system more consistently and developing more of a ‘‘smart pressure’’ style without being reckless.</p><p>‘‘There’s still more room for us to grow and play with the puck and make [more] plays,’’ Mangiapane said. ‘‘But you can see, from where we were at the start of the year to now, we’re winning more puck battles. Our compete level is what’s helping us win these games.’’</p>
entries.author: Ben Pope

entries.title: Elite talents Grant Bowen, Jakobe Baldwin lead IC Catholic to 3A state title
entries.summary: <p>Grant Bowen has spent his entire life around IC Catholic football. His dad, Matt Bowen, played in the NFL and now serves as an assistant coach with the Knights.</p><p>“It’s surreal, being here six years ago as a little child and seeing [IC Catholic win state] in 2022 and then being here now winning it,” Grant Bowen said after the Knights knocked off St. Joseph-Ogden 61-26 in the Class 3A state title game on <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2026/11/26/illinois-high-school-football-state-championship-scores-ihsa" >Friday</a> at ISU’s Hancock Stadium.</p><p>But that story happens every year in Illinois high school sports. It’s not uncommon to see a coach’s kid who watched a successful team grow up and eventually win his own high school title.</p><p>Bowen, a 6-4, 220-pound tight end, is not your typical coach’s kid. The junior is one of the country's top prospects, with more than 30 college scholarship offers.</p><p>That talent showed up nearly every time Bowen touched the ball. He caught four passes, and three went for touchdowns, all from more than 30 yards out.</p><p>And Bowen isn’t IC Catholic’s only elite talent. Running back Jakobe Baldwin is one of the state’s best sophomores. He had 20 carries for 335 yards and four touchdowns.</p><p>“Our offense is like a Swiss Army knife,” Bowen said. “We can do everything.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div entries.title: Bears fans told us what made Revie Sorey more than just an offensive lineman. 'Awesome human'
entries.summary: <p>Chicago Sun-Times readers shared memories of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/27/revie-sorey-bears-guard-blocked-walter-payton-dedicated-life-helping-at-risk-kids-dies-73" target="_blank" >late Chicago Bears offensive lineman Revie Sorey</a>, who helped pave the way for legendary running back Walter Payton. Here is what you told us, lightly edited. </p><p>"I got to meet him at an all-day charity event when I was a kid. The first Chicago Bears player I ever met in person. He was great to us that day, and I'll never forget shaking his hand. Rest easy, sir."<br><i>— Jerry LaBuy</i></p><p>"Lucky enough to meet this awesome human during his playing days. He couldn’t have been nicer to me or all the other fans that day. Rest easy, big fella."<br><i>— Steve Medel Sr.</i></p><p>"Classic player; what a thrill to watch him and Noah Jackson pave the way for Walter (Payton). Prayers."<br>— <i>Philip Doherty</i></p><p>"I was fortunate to work for him at the Hammond Boys & Girls Club. He became a great mentor of mine, and he has always held a special place in my heart. It’s a sad day in my home."<br><i>— Cathie Dull</i></p><p>"He and Noah Jackson came to my elementary school for an assembly. I can’t remember the purpose of the assembly, but the two put on a spectacular display of dunking basketballs on the 8-foot rims."<br><i>— Chris Zima</i></p><p>"I remember meeting him in grade school. He was a down-to-earth guy and was in tune with all of us youngsters." Prayers to his family.'<br><i>— Chris J Vieweg</i></p><p>"Revie’s racquetball tournaments were some of the largest racquetball tournaments played in Illinois. I was fortunate to play with him and against him in a few tournaments. My son also went to Revie's football camps. Rest in peace, Revie."<br>— <i>Patrice Marie</i></p><p>"Just saw this. Linemen for life. He and Noah Jackson were part of our childhood in the 70s."<br><i>— Steven Henkel</i><br></p>

entries.title: Sacred Heart-Griffin's Mikey Groesch scores in OT to beat Morris and win Class 4A
entries.summary: <p>NORMAL, IL — Overtime in a tied state championship game, and Mikey Groesch saw the end zone in front of him. He doesn’t remember much more than that, but he made the 10-yard run to give Sacred Heart-Griffin a 20-14 win over Morris in the Class 4A title game on <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2026/11/26/illinois-high-school-football-state-championship-scores-ihsa" >Friday</a> at ISU’s Hancock Stadium.</p><p>“Words can’t describe my emotions at that point in time,” Groesch said. “I have nothing to say about how that last play went down. I blacked out and tried to celebrate as best I could.”</p><p>The celebration was the best scene in a while in Normal, with one Cyclones player dumping the contents of a cooler on a coach and the coach tackling him.</p><p>“We have been in so many of these games before,” Sacred Heart-Griffin quarterback Cam Brinkman said. “We knew coming into this that if it was close late, we had the confidence to pull it out. We just had to keep within our emotions and stay calm.”</p><p>Cyclones coach John Allison believes those emotions were too high early. Morris jumped out to a 14-0 lead after Ma’rion Persich connected with Max Scritich on a three-yard touchdown pass with 10:22 left in the second quarter.</p><p>Sacred Heart-Griffin (13-1) didn’t allow another point the rest of the way.</p><p>“Part of it was just settling down a bit,” Allison said. “Both sides of the ball started a little bit off. We were doing a better job than it showed early on. [Persich] is a tremendous player and we knew it would be tough to keep him boxed in all night. But there weren’t a ton of changes [in the second half].”</p><p>Morris (13-1) had the ball first in overtime. The Warriors’ possession ended scoreless when senior Austin Rutter picked off a pass from Persich.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure But we can come back next year with the win.”</p><p>Persich had 13 carries for 94 yards and went 6-for-17 for 71 yards passing.</p><p>Groesch finished with 118 rushing yards and two touchdowns. Brinkman had 20 carries for 128 yards and went 4-for-10 for 52 yards passing, with one interception.</p><p>“Congratulations to SHG,” Morris coach Alan Thorson said. “Tremendous game and their kids played with a lot of heart. It is heartbreaking. It is disappointing. This has been a special group for us. These kids played great football all year, and more importantly, they represented our town, our school and our program with tremendous pride and respect with the way they played.”</p><p>This is Sacred Heart-Griffin's seventh state championship. entries.title: Cubs stay busy in free agency with reported addition of lefty reliever Ryan Yarbrough
entries.summary: <p>Seemingly trying to make his post-lockout to-do list as small as possible, Jed Hoyer keeps landing free agents.</p><p>Shortly after news of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/11/27/cubs-hiromi-itoh-mlb-offseason-free-agency-trade-rumors-pitching-staff-starting-rotation-jed-hoyer" >a deal with Japanese pitcher Hiromi Itoh</a>, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> added free-agent reliever Ryan Yarbrough to the back end of their bullpen, according to multiple national reports.</p><p>A lefty-throwing veteran of nine major league seasons, Yarbrough was part of the Yankees’ relief corps in 2026, posting a 3.69 ERA and finishing 19 games, including earning a trio of saves. He also pitched as a part of the U.S. team during this year’s World Baseball Classic alongside Cubs stars Pete Crow-Armstrong and Alex Bregman.</p><p>Though there’s been ample attention on Hoyer’s task of remaking the Cubs’ rotation – what with all five pitchers who finished the 2026 season in the starting staff off to free agency – there’s plenty of work to be done in the bullpen, too, with Hoyer giving himself poor marks for the way he attempted to replicate his 2025 success in constructing last season’s relief unit.</p><p>“I did a poor job on the bullpen this year, full stop,” Hoyer said during his end-of-season press conference last month. “Last year, I was really proud of our bullpen, in 2025. It was a huge part of our success last year. We built the bullpen with the same philosophy or the same thoughts in mind. We didn’t get it right, and that’s something we’ve spent a lot of time talking about already and we’ll continue to talk about.</p><p>“I take responsibility for that, and it’s something we’ll look to improve on this offseason.”</p><p>The addition of Yarbrough can be counted as part of that project, certainly the highest profile part to date, though there have been several smaller moves, as well.</p><p>Right-handers Eric Orze and Chayce McDermott were claimed off waivers, with the Cubs making a trade with the Nationals for right-hander Braxton Roby.</p><p>Additionally, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/11/02/cubs-jacob-webb-contract-free-agency-mlb-offseason-bullpen-jed-hoyer" >they gave a new contract to righty Jacob Webb</a>, who was their best relief pitcher for a good stretch of the summer after joining as a free agent last offseason. With right-hander Daniel Palencia injured, Webb stepped into the role of go-to reliever and closer, at one point turning in 24 consecutive scoreless appearances, though some memorable late-season blow-ups tarnished what was an otherwise excellent campaign.</p><p>With <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/11/24/cubs-free-agents-trevor-rogers-teruaki-sato-jed-hoyer-mlb-offseason-contract-salary-payroll-trade-rumors" >free-agent deals</a> for lefty starter Trevor Rogers, Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, Itoh and now Yarbrough, Hoyer is crossing some big items off a packed offseason to-do list. He’s in the middle of remaking the Cubs’ pitching staff and has a couple more holes to plug in the lineup. There’s still a lot left to do, and the looming lockout is expected to bring the sport to a screeching halt Dec. 2.</p><p>Hoyer will be unable to do any roster construction with baseball on pause, and he and every other team will be sent scrambling to put their rosters together whenever the work stoppage is over.</p><p>In other words, the more he gets done in these final days, the better position the Cubs will be in.</p>

entries.title: Man dies after being found with gunshot wounds in Grand Boulevard
entries.summary: <p>A man died after being found in a South Side neighborhood Friday night, Chicago police said.</p><p>The unidentified man was found with multiple gunshot wounds in the 4600 block of South Federal Street in the Grand Boulevard neighborhood at 8 p.m., Chicago police said. </p><p>He was taken to University of Chicago Medical Center in critical condition, where he later died, police said. </p><p>Area 1 detectives are investigating. </p>

entries.title: Cubs’ pitching staff gets another free-agent boost with reported deal for Japanese righty Hiromi Itoh
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> keep on adding in the days before Major League Baseball’s expected lockout.</p><p>In the wake of $120 million deals for <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/11/24/cubs-trevor-rogers-mlb-offseason-free-agents-rumors-pitching-starting-rotation-2027" >lefty pitcher Trevor Rogers</a> and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/11/24/cubs-teruaki-sato-mlb-offseason-free-agents-rumors-outfield-third-base-jed-hoyer-contract-salary" >Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato</a>, the Cubs went back to the free-agent well to add Japanese pitcher Hiromi Itoh, according to multiple national reports.</p><p>Itoh, a 29-year-old right-hander, comes to the U.S. after six seasons with the Nippon Ham Fighters, a tenure during which he won that league’s equivalent of the Cy Young Award.</p><p>He had back-to-back fantastic campaigns in 2024 and 2025, posting ERAs of 2.65 and 2.52, respectively, and striking out 356 batters in a combined 373 innings. In 2026, Itoh finished with a 3.18 ERA in 172 2/3 innings.</p><p>Itoh is known for his ability to limit free passes and issued fewer than 40 walks in each of the last three seasons, including just 34 in 2026. Of the 32 major league pitchers who threw at least 170 innings this year, only two issued fewer walks than 34. Itoh issued only 29 walks in 196 2/3 innings in 2025, something no major leaguer managed that season.</p><p>It’s the latest step in team president Jed Hoyer’s effort to remake the Cubs’ pitching staff this offseason.</p><p>With all five pitchers who ended last season in the starting rotation off to free agency, Hoyer has already restocked with Rogers, who got a five-year deal to become part of the team’s long-term core, and now Itoh, helping to fortify against the question marks that hang over in-house arms Cade Horton, Justin Steele and Ben Brown, all coming off significant injuries.</p><p>Itoh, of course, will bring his own questions about his ability to transfer his success in Japan to the major leagues, though the Cubs have had their own recent success making that happen with lefty pitcher Shota Imanaga and outfielder Seiya Suzuki.</p><p>Like that duo, who teamed on the North Side for a half decade, Itoh and Sato form another Japanese pairing the Cubs are hoping helps them close the gap with the world-champion Brewers, who finished 14 games ahead in the NL Central standings last season.</p><p>Part of Hoyer’s effort to get closer to the Brewers is improving his team’s pitching staff, which stood as the clear area in need of attention after the Cubs finished the regular season with baseball’s highest scoring offense and far and away its best defense.</p><p>Itoh represents the latest bit of work on that front, though it’s a big project that will require a lot more than two new arms, no matter how high profile on this winter’s free-agent market. Rogers was arguably the No. 2 pitcher available after two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, who got a record-setting $450 million from the Mets, while Itoh was one of a few notable players arriving from Japan this offseason, Sato the highest profile of that group.</p><p>Hoyer’s front office keeps swimming in deep free-agent waters with the work it’s doing this winter, combining with last offseason’s $175 million deal for third baseman Alex Bregman to smash the narrative about the big-market Cubs not spending like a big-market team.</p>
